children: Crypto markets entered the week under pressure, with
Bitcoin
falling sharply and fear spreading across digital assets. Investors also faced renewed debate over long-term price targets and institutional participation. Meanwhile,
Dogecoin
outlined a broader technology roadmap, while industry figures weighed regulatory hurdles and the possibility of deeper losses across the market.
Peter Schiff Sees Bitcoin Risk Below $16,500
Economist and longtime Bitcoin critic
Peter Schiff

said Saturday that Bitcoin’s decline could gather speed if the cryptocurrency falls below $50,000. From there, he said, the price could quickly revisit its 2022 low, below $16,500. Schiff made the comments in a post on X as Bitcoin’s selling momentum continued. His warning also placed renewed attention on losses tied to Strategy holdings, according to the report.
Crypto Market Sinks Into Extreme Fear

Bitcoin dropped to $66,500, representing a 23% decline from its October peak, while the total cryptocurrency market capitalization fell from nearly $3 trillion to $2.3 trillion. Most major altcoins also remained in a deep bear market. The crypto Fear and Greed Index declined to 17, signaling extreme fear, while the CNN Money Fear and Greed Index moved into the fear zone at 39.
Bitcoin’s $1 Million Target Faces Skepticism
Haseeb Qureshi
, managing partner at
Dragonfly Capital

, said Bitcoin could reach between $300,000 and $400,000 by 2030. However, he dismissed the likelihood of a $1 million price. Qureshi said achieving that milestone would require an enormous inflow of capital. Asked whether Bitcoin could reach $1 million by 2030, he responded, "Almost certainly not."
Dogecoin Expands Beyond Its Meme-Coin Roots
Dogecoin
could broaden its role beyond payments and meme-driven trading through DogeOS, an ecosystem designed to support decentralized finance, prediction markets and gaming applications.
Timothy Stebbing

, Dogecoin’s director of product, shared the ecosystem’s 2026 roadmap in an X post Nov. 11. The plan highlights smart contracts and artificial intelligence while preserving Dogecoin’s core blockchain.
Kevin O’Leary Calls For Crypto Regulatory Clarity
Veteran investor
Kevin O’Leary

said the recent cryptocurrency sell-off reflects institutional hesitation, not simply weakness in Bitcoin. He argued that broader market concerns extend across digital assets. O’Leary said passage of the
CLARITY Act
and other regulatory guidance is necessary before more companies commit to digital-asset infrastructure. He made the comments while sharing a clip from his interview with
FINTECH TV
